asA: verifier at the TEST stage on a TypeScript product
iWant: test strength to run each bound test through its declared runner and read that runner's report
soThat: TypeScript criteria get the proof JavaScript criteria get
description: RC-46, round D (0.39.0): TypeScript test strength. Bound tests under tsx node:test, vitest and @playwright/test, each run through its declared runner and judged from that runner's report; Code Nodes in .ts, .tsx and .vue files; what stays unreadable reported per criterion as BLOCKED.
title: The verifier runs test strength over TypeScript bound tests through each test's declared runner and its report

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given a fixture whose `rcf/test-strength.json` declares entry `src/index.ts` and no runner, and whose AC-101-1 is bound to `test/totals.test.ts::sums the line items` (node:test inside one describe, importing `../src/index.ts`) and claims the typed function `src/totals.ts#sumTotals`, when `rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1` runs, then it exits 0 with stdout "test-strength: PASS 1 criteria at <h7>: structural 1/1, mutants killed 2/2 (timeout 0, notApplicable 1)", and likewise under a tsx `runners` entry; and the same PASS under that tsx `runners` entry when the bound test imports its `.ts` source through a NodeNext `.js` specifier (a test importing `../../../../src/intervals.js` for the declared entry `src/intervals.ts`, AC-101-1 bound to its describe title and claiming `src/intervals.ts#overlaps`).

[happy] Given a vitest `runners` entry and AC-101-1 bound to `test/cart.test.ts::cart > applies a percentage discount`, importing `../src/index`, claiming `src/cart.ts#applyDiscount`, when the audit runs, then it exits 0, structural 1/1, both body mutants killed. A pointer may also name a describe title (`<file>::<describe title>`): it matches as a prefix of the report's title path (`ancestorTitles` then `title`), the bound test counts as run when at least one leaf under it ran, and as failed under a mutant when any leaf under it failed, the node:test treatment; so a vitest `runners` entry with AC-101-1 bound to a describe title `tests/rcf/unit/US-101/AC-101-1.spec.ts::AC-101-1: <summary>` and claiming `src/slug.ts#slugify` and `src/slug.ts#isSlug` exits 0 with the PASS line, structural 1/1.

[happy] Given a playwright `runners` entry and `e2e/slug.spec.ts::slug > slugs a title`, a spec using no browser fixture, when the audit runs, then it exits 0 and each mutant of `src/slug.ts#slugify` reads killed. Each bound test file runs under the first `runners` entry whose `files` glob matches it, so one criterion bound to a vitest test and a Playwright test runs each under its own entry (the same criterion also bound to `test/slug.test.ts::slug > joins the words of a title with hyphens` under a vitest entry passes the same way); no match falls to the legacy `runner` with today's exit-code rule, else kind nodeTest. `rcf audit test-strength --help` documents the `runners` field of `rcf/test-strength.json` beside the legacy `runner`: a list of entries `{ "files": [glob], "kind": "nodeTest" | "vitest" | "playwright", "argv": [...] }`, first match wins, and an entry that matches no bound file is allowed and silent; `kind` sets the default argv and the report the verb reads, `argv` overrides it. Each kind's default argv carries the reporter the audit reads: nodeTest the TAP reporter, vitest and playwright their JSON reporter. The default argv of each kind (the stage-keeper's ruling Q3): nodeTest today's array with `--test-reporter=tap` inserted after `--test` (`node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern <name> <file>`); vitest `vitest run <file> -t <name> --reporter=json --outputFile=<report>`; playwright `playwright test <file> -g <name> --reporter=json`. The audit adds no flag to a runner's argv: each kind's default argv runs as stated here and an `argv` override as written, an override naming its own cache flags included; what a runner writes under node_modules stays in the audit's working copy (AC-19903-5). `<report>` is a per-run temp path the audit sets and reads, and an `argv` override may name `<report>` (the stage-keeper's ruling F2). The name filter of each kind (the stage-keeper's ruling F1): nodeTest `--test-name-pattern` with `<name>` an escaped `^name$`, as today; vitest `-t` with the titles joined by " > ", a leaf as `(^| > )<leaf>$` (anchored at the end and at a title boundary, so a nested test runs and a longer title ending in the same words does not), a full path as `^<titles joined by " > ">$`, the leaf and title text regex-escaped, `^prefix` with no `$` for a describe prefix, and the report's space-joined `fullName` mapped back to the titles, never split on spaces; playwright `-g` with the segments space-joined, `$`-anchored for a leaf or a full path, and for a describe prefix followed by a space with no `$` (the describe prefix joins with a space), never `^`. `files` globs follow the glob grammar the audit already applies to `harness` ("**" spans directories, "*" and "?" stay inside one segment); an entry is malformed when `files` is missing, empty, or not an array of non-empty strings, `kind` is not one of the three, or `argv`, when given, lacks both the `<file>` and the `<name>` placeholder; a malformed entry exits 2 with a stderr line starting "test-strength: malformed rcf/test-strength.json" that names the entry's index (`runners[<i>]`). An `argv` override replaces the whole argv and must carry its own reporter flag: given a vitest entry whose `argv` carries no reporter flag, the audit cannot read the report, so the unmutated run fails, exit 2, with today's unmutated-run line and a hint on its own stderr line after the unmutated-run line, naming the flag (`--reporter`; nodeTest `--test-reporter`).

[happy] Given Code Nodes `src/Badge.tsx#badgeLabel`, `src/Counter.vue#clampStart` (in `<script lang="ts">`) and file-level `src/Counter.vue` under vitest, when the audit runs, then it exits 0, each symbol has three mutants and the SFC one fileBlank. Given instead the Code Node `src/Counter.vue#clampStart` in a two-block SFC whose `<script setup lang="ts">` block and template come first and whose `<script lang="ts">` block declaring it comes last, the audit exits 0 with three mutants on it. The SFC script view (the stage-keeper's ruling Q9): concatenate every `<script>` and `<script setup>` block (lang ts, tsx or js; attributes otherwise ignored) in document order, non-script content replaced by blank lines so line numbers hold; a block with a `src` attribute is unsupported and makes the criterion BLOCKED with the detail form AC-19901-9 states (`<file>:<line>:<col>: <construct>`). The JSX scan of a .tsx file (the stage-keeper's ruling Q8): accepted: elements, self-closing elements, fragments, attributes (string, expression container, spread), expression containers with nested JSX, text, comments inside containers. Failure: any unbalanced tag, brace or container the scanner cannot close, or a construct outside that list; failure is recorded as AC-19904-7 rules (its `detail` "JSX scan failed at <file>:<line>:<col>: <what the scanner met>") and never a guess.

[failure] Given a vitest pointer whose name matches no test in its file, when the audit runs, then it exits 2 with "test-strength: bound test <file>::<name> was not run by runner <argv>" and scores no mutant.

[failure] Given a `.ts` bound test importing `vitest` that matches no `runners` entry, with no `runner`, when the audit runs, then it prints today's unmutated-run line plus "declare a runner for <file> in rcf/test-strength.json runners" and exits 2. The hint fires when a bound file has no matching `runners` entry and is .ts, .mts, .cts, .tsx, .jsx or .vue, or its source imports vitest or @playwright/test; plain .js and .mjs files default to nodeTest silently.

[failure] Given a Code Node file holding a TypeScript enum (`src/totals.ts` declaring `export enum Rounding` beside `sumTotals`, its Code Node `src/totals.ts#sumTotals`), when the audit runs (`rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1 --record` at a reviewed head), then that criterion is reported as stage-keeper ruling Q2 (a) rules, BLOCKED, naming the file and "non-erasable TypeScript syntax": its criterion in the TestStrengthReport carries `result` "blocked", `reason` "TEST_STRENGTH_UNSUPPORTED" and a `detail` in the one wording of the stage-keeper's ruling F6, `<file>:<line>:<col>: non-erasable TypeScript syntax (<construct>)`, here naming `src/totals.ts` and the enum, and the TestStrengthReport's own `result` reads "blocked" (none fails and at least one is blocked) and its `totals.blocked` reads 1; a bound test file strip mode refuses blocks its criterion with the same detail, and an entry point so held exits 2 "entry point unreadable" with the same detail. `<line>` and `<col>` are 1-based and place the first character of the construct in the file as committed: `<line>` counts the line breaks before it, a line break being CRLF, a lone CR or LF (U+2028 and U+2029 are not line breaks); `<col>` counts UTF-16 code units from the start of that line, a tab, a form feed, a vertical tab, a byte order mark and a combining mark one unit each and a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane two. For a construct strip mode refuses or a syntax error, that is the construct node's refusal places, whatever characters precede it on the line; where code points of no display width share node's column, the construct is the first of them node does not pass over (a zero-width code point node refuses is itself the construct; one node passes over is not); when the input ends inside a construct (an unclosed bracket, string, template literal or block comment), it is where the innermost such construct opens. When node names a line and no column (the input ends with nothing open), the refusal is placed at that line, column 1. When the audit cannot check the position node gives (the position check is withheld: node's caret does not move across the code points that share its column, as after an escape character, or node's own probes of them disagree), the refusal is placed at node's line, column node's caret index plus 1, and one stderr line names the reason, "test-strength: column for <file>:<line> is node's display column (position check withheld: <reason>)": a documented degraded state, never a silent one, which relaxes none of the positions above for an input node places. A `.vue` file's position counts in the `.vue` file, and a `.tsx` or `.jsx` file's JSX scan failure by the same rule. A `.tsx` Code Node file the JSX scan cannot read is recorded the same way, its detail naming the file and the scan failure, `detail` "JSX scan failed at <file>:<line>:<col>: <what the scanner met>"; the summary line reads "test-strength: BLOCKED <n> criteria at <h7>: structural a/b, mutants killed x/y (timeout t, notApplicable n, blocked m): <id> (<file>), <id> (<file>)"; the run exits 5, the BLOCKED exit (exit 1 is the bin's unexpected-failure code); when a run has both a blocked and a failing criterion the fail verdict and its exit code win: the verdict word is FAIL, the FAIL line gains ", blocked <m>: <id> (<file>), ..." at its end, and the summary line still counts the blocked criteria and lists their ids; and light Finalise refuses it like a fail, exit 4 with "finalise refused: test-strength at <H7> fails for AC-101-1". Ids in ascending criterion-id order, comma and space separated, each file relative to the repo root; a criterion with several blocked files lists each file after the id, joined by " and ". On the BLOCKED and FAIL lines `<n>` and "of <n>" are the criteria in scope (totals.criteria); a is structuralPassed and b is the criteria in scope less the blocked ones; x/y are counted as on the PASS line; m is the blocked criteria (the stage-keeper's ruling F7). A blocked criterion carries structural { checked: false }, mutants [] and blocked: true beside result, contributes zero to every mutant count of totals, and counts in neither structuralPassed nor killed.

[edge] Given a runners entry with `"cwd": "project"`, when the audit runs, then its tests run at the rcf project root with project-relative `<file>` (a bound test in `apps/api` reading a path relative to the rcf project root runs green: exit 0 with the PASS line).

[happy] Given a nodeTest runners entry whose argv starts with a bare `tsx` installed in the test's package, or the legacy `runner` whose argv starts with a bare `tsx` installed only in the repository root's `node_modules/.bin`, when the audit runs from a shell whose PATH holds no `node_modules/.bin`, then the test runs (exit 0 with the PASS line, no "cannot run the bound tests" line). Every `node_modules/.bin` from the test's package directory up to the repository root joins the PATH of its bound test run, nearest first, ahead of the inherited PATH, for every runner kind (a nodeTest, vitest or playwright `runners` entry and the legacy `runner`) and for a `runners` entry with `"cwd": "project"`.

[failure] Given an `rcf/test-strength.json` whose `runners` entry at index `<i>` carries a `"cwd"` key whose value is anything other than the string `"project"` (another string such as `"package"`, `null`, a number), when `rcf audit test-strength` runs, then it exits 2 as a malformed config with a stderr line starting "test-strength: malformed rcf/test-strength.json" that names `runners[<i>].cwd`, as the audit names the other fields of a malformed `runners` entry (exit 2 and that stderr line).

[failure] Given a bound test whose unmutated run is red, such as a test in `apps/api` that reads a path relative to the rcf project root with no `runners` entry pinning `"cwd": "project"` for it, when `rcf audit test-strength` runs, then the stderr line right after the unmutated-run line reads "test-strength: <file> ran at <cwd>; a test that reads paths relative to the rcf project root pins "cwd": "project" on its runners entry", `<file>` the bound test file and `<cwd>` the directory its run ran at, each a path relative to the rcf project root (`.` for the rcf project root itself; `apps/api/test/root.test.mjs` and `apps/api` for that test), and the unmutated-run line stays exactly as AC-19902-9 states it (exit 2, the unmutated-run line, then that hint line).

[failure] Given a bound test whose runner opens a Unix socket under its TMPDIR (tsx at `<TMPDIR>/tsx-<uid>/<pid>.pipe`, as under AC-19904-1's tsx `runners` entry), when `rcf audit test-strength` runs with a temp directory (`tmpdir()`) long enough that `tmpdir()` plus the scratch suffix (the scratch directory `rcf-ts-<6 chars>` and a runner's socket path under it) would pass the platform's limit for a Unix socket path, 104 bytes on darwin and 108 on Linux, then each runner's scratch directory, which is its TMPDIR, moves to a short path, `/tmp/rcf-<6 chars>` on darwin and on Linux alike, the run goes on as AC-19904-1 states it (exit 0 and its PASS line), and the run's first stderr line, printed once per run, reads "test-strength: a runner's Unix socket path under <tmpdir> would pass <limit> bytes, the limit on <platform>; the scratch directory moves to a short path", `<tmpdir>` the temp directory, `<limit>` 104 or 108 and `<platform>` darwin or linux; under a temp directory short enough, the scratch directory stays under it and no such line prints. 0.40.0 kept the scratch under the long temp directory, tsx failed with "listen EINVAL" and the unmutated run was red (exit 2).
